title: Mooncakes Sell Only Two Months a Year, Yet Build a 28.2 Billion Yuan Business
dek: Bound to Mid-Autumn Festival, mooncakes are trapped in a short sales window, but the 28.2 billion yuan scale comes from gift-giving scenarios and flexible custom production lines, not from flavor innovation.
why: Worth listening for food industry practitioners and those wanting to understand holiday consumer business, but information density is low, with much time spent on explaining factions and flavors, while the business mechanics are concentrated in the middle and later sections.
who: Food industry entrepreneurs, brands doing corporate custom gifts, investors wanting to understand holiday consumer business logic.
skip: 0:12-2:03 Chat about personal taste preferences and Taiwan date paste cakes, unrelated to business analysis.

points.h: Zongzi can be sold year-round, mooncakes cannot
points.body: Zongzi is tied to Dragon Boat Festival, but after vacuum-sealing for long shelf life, it can be sold all year round. Wufangzhai even opened restaurants to put zongzi into daily scenarios. The problem with mooncakes is not that the craft cannot achieve long shelf life, but that it is defined as a "traditional festival pastry mainly eaten during Mid-Autumn Festival," and the national standard GB19855 directly writes the season into the definition. So for the same festival food, zongzi can decouple from the festival through shelf life and channels, but mooncakes cannot.

points.h: National standard draws hard lines for fillings
points.body: Lotus seed paste mooncakes must have at least 60% lotus seed content, fruit mooncakes must have at least 25% fruit products, and five-kernel mooncakes must use walnut kernels, almond kernels, olive kernels, melon seed kernels, and sesame seeds. The purpose of this line is to raise ingredient costs and prevent cheap candied winter melon, green and red shreds, and inferior nuts from being used as fillers. For consumers, the order of ingredients on the label can indicate how much is used.

points.h: Why custard lava mooncakes are made so small
points.body: Custard lava mooncakes are small not because of stinginess, but because of structure. They have a flaky crust outside, a custard layer in the middle, and a lava layer at the center. The custard layer acts as a moisture barrier. Production requires two rounds of baking to keep the lava semi-solid, and the melting point of the lava must be designed—solid during transport, and after a few seconds in the microwave, it becomes a flowing liquid. If overheated, the lava is absorbed by the crust, and it reverts to an ordinary custard mooncake.

points.h: Five prerequisites for everything to become mooncake
points.body: Not everything can be stuffed into a mooncake. First is water content: hot and sour soup mooncake cannot be made because there is too much water to wrap. Second is safety: meat, eggs, and dairy are also loved by microorganisms, so processing temperature and sterilization processes must be repeatedly tested. Third is particle size: too large and the crust cannot hold it, too fine and it cannot be tasted. Fourth is flavor restoration after high-temperature baking: some aromas disappear after baking. Fifth is whether the cost can be handled. So long-term stable flavors are confirmed by generations.

points.h: Choosing an OEM is not about the biggest
points.body: When big brands make brand mooncakes and look for OEMs, there is a common misconception: they must choose the best OEM in China. But the production scale of top OEMs actually does not match yours. Indicators that can be screened include registered capital, tax payment records, number of employees with social security contributions, and accumulated safe production days. In addition, the nine major factions correspond to different factories; it is impossible to have Guangzhou Restaurant produce Shanxi egg-skin mooncakes, as they do not have the capability or production line.

points.h: Flexible production lines can take orders of a few hundred boxes
points.body: Mooncake production is semi-automated and semi-manual. The wrapping and shaping machines can do the work, but brushing egg wash, pressing patterns, and stamping require manual labor, which actually facilitates OEM and customization. Flexible factories can go as small as a few hundred boxes, and can do thousands or tens of thousands of boxes. If a company has only 50 employees, they can directly use the factory's existing mooncakes and only need to design the paper box. This small-order quick-response capability is the core of mooncakes being able to do corporate custom business.

points.h: The 28.2 billion scale is supported by gift-giving
points.body: In 2025, China's mooncake production was 518,000 tons, with sales scale of 28.2 billion RMB, both down from the previous year. At 80 grams each, that is about 6.4 billion pieces; at 100 grams, about 5.18 billion pieces. With a population of 1.4 billion, that averages three to four pieces per person. In comparison, Dragon Boat Festival zongzi annual sales scale is about 10 to 11 billion, and instant noodles about 68 to 120 billion. Mooncakes selling only two months a year to achieve 28.2 billion is core to gift-giving attributes—brands prepare large amounts of PR gifts at the two nodes of Chinese New Year and Mid-Autumn Festival, and zongzi's gift-giving attribute is far weaker than mooncakes.

points.h: 499 yuan is a number forced by regulatory line
points.body: In 2022, the National Development and Reform Commission and three other departments jointly issued an announcement to implement key supervision on boxed mooncakes priced over 500 yuan per unit. So the highest price of mooncakes on the market is 499. The calculation logic is: a box of mooncakes costs about 70 yuan per box, plus channel deductions and shared expenses, it cannot exceed 500 yuan. In the past when the economy was good, there were sky-high mooncakes with very expensive tea or liquor, even wooden gift boxes, and both cost and price were very high.

points.h: Mini package is becoming a trend
points.body: In the food industry, there has been an obvious trend in the past two years called mini package, where packaging is made smaller. On one hand, it can be finished in one go after opening; on the other hand, consumers just want a quick treat and do not want to eat that much, and small packaging also allows buying many flavors at once. Mooncakes are also moving in this direction because it is hard for one person to finish a whole mooncake, usually cut into several pieces to share. Making them smaller means one person can at least finish one, and it also reduces waste.

points.h: New flavors die before reaching consumers
points.body: Brands launch five new flavors each year to see which gets eliminated, but a flavor not being repurchased is not necessarily because consumers dislike it; it might not have reached consumers at all. Because most mooncakes are gifts, they keep being regifted, and the recipient may not even eat it before passing it on. So next year, they will not want to buy that flavor because they did not taste it this year. Brands with physical stores have the advantage of offering tastings, letting consumers try before deciding.

quotes.text: I think we have cakes and pastries 365 days a year, it's just that what we usually eat isn't called mooncake.
It's not that everything can be forced into a mooncake. A long-term stable flavor is definitely confirmed by generations of people to be OK.
This large OEM's production scale actually doesn't match yours.
If it breaks away from the Mid-Autumn period, or breaks away from the round shape, it's actually just a pastry.
A flavor that doesn't get repurchased isn't necessarily disliked by consumers; it might not have reached consumers at all.
Brands and channels no longer want to consider making a long-term classic that lasts forever; what they want is rapid iteration.
